name: minecraft_run
description: Do all world work here: inspect your body, inventory, entities, players and blocks, then move, mine, place, craft, use items and menus, chat and run commands, as one awaited JavaScript procedure using your body's bot API. Prefer one script per meaningful step over many small calls. The body stays under script control between steps. Returns the script's JSON result and logs. Permissions and physical limits still apply; no automatic retry after uncertain outcomes. API coverage is in the scripting instructions.

name: minecraft_settings
description: Read your body's mod settings: name, species, game mode (survival, creative, creative_commands), activity behaviors, the box you must stay inside, and capabilities.

name: minecraft_observe
description: Observe body, nearby entities, live player, inventory, settings and current action. Radius 1–64.

name: minecraft_pov
description: Capture a rendered PNG from your NPC body's eyes without moving the human camera. Returns the saved file's absolute path. Open it with your image-viewing tool to see the snapshot.

name: minecraft_blocks
description: Inspect a loaded inclusive block box, at most 4096 blocks.

name: minecraft_action
description: Start one physical intention. Walk/look target position or entity UUID/'player'. Mine position; place clicks supporting block position+face using held item. Equip inventory slot; creative_item item/count; pickup nearby or approach item entity/position; give entity/item/count; interact position/face or entity; menu inspect; menu_click menuId/slot/button/clickType; menu_close. Inspect results. Returns action ID; poll status. Local native control approaches targets. No retry on unknown outcome.

name: minecraft_action_status
description: Read current or historical action, without repeating it.

name: minecraft_cancel
description: Stop your current physical action or a specified ID.

name: minecraft_command
description: Run a Minecraft command only in creative_commands mode, using the human's existing permissions. @s is your body.

name: screen_list
description: List the screens you can use, `limit` at a time (`truncated` counts the rest; raise `limit` if you don't find what you need). Your station's screens come first, marked `yours`. Screens linked to any other station, occupied or free, aren't listed and can't be used; a free station's screens wait for an agent spawned there. Shared screens follow, nearest you or the user first, with screens in other dimensions last. `distance` is how far each screen is from the user and from you, useful for telling screens apart, e.g. when the user says 'over here' or 'by you'. `openedByYou` marks pages you opened, including in earlier turns. Each row has a stable UUID `id` and a unique readable `name`. Names can change; keep the UUID for future calls. Pickup ends that identity. A `lease` identifies the thread currently controlling the screen.

limit.description: Most rows to return. Default 20, at most 50.

name: screen_open
description: Show something on a screen: a URL, or a file path. Waits for the page to load (up to about 15s), then returns `{ screen, url, title }`. Screens always have a unique name. Rename one when its name no longer describes what you are using it for; otherwise leave it alone.

screen.description: Screen UUID or unique name (case-insensitive). Prefer the UUID for lasting references; it survives renaming, but not pickup and replacement. Omit to use your station's only screen. A screen linked to any other station, occupied or free, fails with `no_access`.

target.description: URL, or file path (relative paths resolve from your working directory).

name.description: Unique nonblank name, at most 32 characters. Names are reserved across the world, including unloaded screens, ignoring capitalization. Omit to keep the name.

name: screen_cdp
description: A plain Chrome DevTools Protocol passthrough to a screen's page. To run JS: `Runtime.evaluate { expression, awaitPromise: true, returnByValue: true }`. Returns the method's result plus the current `{ url, title }`. One call, one result; events aren't streamed. Results are capped at about 64 KB (use `screen_screenshot` for images). Times out after about 30s. Fails with `unavailable` on an idle screen.

screen.description: Screen UUID or unique name (case-insensitive). Prefer the UUID for lasting references; it survives renaming, but not pickup and replacement. Omit to use your station's only screen. A screen linked to any other station, occupied or free, fails with `no_access`.

name: screen_screenshot
description: Capture the frame already painted for a screen, at its viewport size. Saves the PNG and returns `{ path, url, title }`; open the path with your image tool. Doesn't need the lease. Fails with `unavailable` on an idle screen.

screen.description: Screen UUID or unique name (case-insensitive). Prefer the UUID for lasting references; it survives renaming, but not pickup and replacement. Omit to use your station's only screen. A screen linked to any other station, occupied or free, fails with `no_access`.

name: screen_close
description: Close a screen's page so it goes idle. Its id, name and station link stay, and a later `screen_open` brings it back. Releases your lease.

screen.description: Screen UUID or unique name (case-insensitive). Prefer the UUID for lasting references; it survives renaming, but not pickup and replacement. Omit to use your station's only screen. A screen linked to any other station, occupied or free, fails with `no_access`.
